findings.title: Sensitive user data stored in browser localStorage without encryption
findings.description: User credentials and profile information (user_id, user_role, user_name, user_email) are stored in plain text in localStorage. This violates secure token storage practices and exposes sensitive data to XSS attacks and malicious scripts.

locations.snippet:
localStorage.setItem('user_id', data.session.user.id)
localStorage.setItem('user_role', profile!.role)
localStorage.setItem('user_name', profile!.name)
localStorage.setItem('user_email', profile!.email)

public name: string = localStorage.getItem('user_name') || ''
email: string = localStorage.getItem('user_email') || ''
id: string = localStorage.getItem('user_id') || ''
created_by: localStorage.getItem('user_id') || ""

findings.suggested_fix: Replace localStorage with Supabase session management. Use Supabase's built-in session handling which stores tokens in secure, HTTP-only cookies. Remove all manual localStorage.setItem() calls and instead retrieve user data from Supabase's getSession() or getUser() methods. Store only non-sensitive identifiers if needed, and never store role/email in localStorage. Example: const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession(); // Use session.user directly instead of localStorage

findings.title: Missing token refresh mechanism and session expiration validation
findings.description: The application uses Supabase JWT tokens but does not implement automatic token refresh or validate token expiration before making API calls. Expired tokens will silently fail, causing poor UX and potential security gaps where stale sessions remain active.

locations.snippet: // File exists but full implementation not shown - need to verify token refresh logic

findings.suggested_fix: Implement token refresh in the Supabase service. Add a method to refresh the session before expiration: async refreshSessionIfNeeded() { const { data: { session } } = await this.supabase.auth.getSession(); if (session && this.isTokenExpiringSoon(session)) { await this.supabase.auth.refreshSession(); } }. Call this method in authGuard before checking user permissions. Consider using Supabase's built-in onAuthStateChange() to automatically handle token refresh events.

findings.title: Insufficient role-based access control in auth guard
findings.description: The authGuard checks if roles array exists and has length > 0, but requires roles to be explicitly defined in route data. Routes without defined roles default to denying access (returning false), but this creates an error state rather than graceful handling. More critically, there's no validation that profile.role actually matches UserRole enum values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add enum validation and fix the guard logic: (1) Validate that profile.role is a valid UserRole enum value before casting: if (!Object.values(UserRole).includes(profile.role)) { await supabase.signOut(); router.navigate(['/login']); return false; } (2) For routes without roles defined, should either deny with error logging or allow publicly. Current implicit deny is confusing. (3) Add logging when role mismatch occurs for audit purposes: console.warn(`Unauthorized access attempt: user ${user.id} with role ${profile.role} tried to access ${route.data['roles']}`);

findings.title: No CSRF protection on form submissions
findings.description: The login form and other POST operations (product creation, mismatch resolution) use HTTP methods without visible CSRF token validation. While Supabase may provide backend protection, frontend-level CSRF tokens are not implemented or validated.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSRF protection using Angular's built-in HttpClientXsrfModule. In app.config.ts, add: provideHttpClientXsrfProtection() and configure the token header/param names. Ensure all POST/PUT/DELETE requests include the X-XSRF-TOKEN header. This is typically handled automatically by Angular if properly configured in the HTTP interceptor. Verify Supabase client is using Angular HttpClient with XSRF interceptor enabled.

findings.title: Hardcoded role checks without centralized authorization service
findings.description: Role-based access is checked in multiple components using hardcoded string comparisons (e.g., 'admin', 'sales'). This scattered logic makes it difficult to audit and maintain authorization rules, and there's no centralized policy enforcement.

locations.snippet:
<!-- Admin Section -->
        <ng-container *ngIf="userRole === 'admin'">

findings.suggested_fix: Create a centralized authorization service: export class AuthorizationService { hasRole(requiredRole: UserRole): boolean { return this.getCurrentUserRole() === requiredRole; } canAccess(feature: string): boolean { const userRole = this.getCurrentUserRole(); const rolePermissions = { [UserRole.admin]: ['inventory', 'staff', 'products'], [UserRole.sales]: ['sales_dashboard'] }; return rolePermissions[userRole]?.includes(feature) || false; } } Inject this service into components instead of checking localStorage directly. Use it in templates as *ngIf="authService.hasRole(UserRole.admin)"

findings.title: No protection against account enumeration via login endpoint
findings.description: The login component shows detailed error messages that could allow attackers to enumerate valid user accounts (e.g., 'Login failed: User not found' vs 'Login failed: Invalid password').
findings.suggested_fix: Use generic error messages for login failures: if (error) { this.toast.show('Invalid email or password', 'error'); return; } Do not expose whether the email exists or if the password is wrong. Log detailed errors server-side only for debugging purposes. This prevents account enumeration attacks while maintaining good UX.

findings.title: Disabled user accounts not immediately revoked on login
findings.description: While the code checks if profile.is_active is false and signs out the user, it still allows them to proceed to role-based routing before the check happens. The check occurs after session creation, not as part of the authentication flow.
findings.suggested_fix: The logic is actually correct, but should be moved earlier or used in conjunction with Supabase RLS policies. Ensure database Row Level Security (RLS) policies on all sensitive tables enforce is_active = true. This way, even if a disabled user somehow gets past frontend checks, they cannot access data. Also consider: (1) calling getRLS-protected endpoints before showing dashboard, (2) implementing automatic logout if is_active becomes false during session (already done in app.component.ts with realtime subscription)

findings.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP) headers
findings.description: No Content Security Policy is defined in index.html or server configuration. This leaves the application vulnerable to XSS attacks and allows arbitrary script execution.

locations.snippet:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">

<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>FrostflowApp</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="favicon.ico" />
    <!-- Missing: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" ...> -->

findings.suggested_fix: Add CSP meta tag to index.html: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;">. Additionally, configure CSP in server headers (Nginx/Docker) for better enforcement. Review and restrict external CDN dependencies (Chart.js from CDN should ideally be bundled).

findings.title: Automatic logout service may not properly invalidate tokens
findings.description: The auto-logout.service is referenced but not shown in provided code. If it relies only on client-side timers without backend session invalidation, tokens could remain valid server-side even after logout.

locations.snippet: // File not provided - cannot verify implementation

findings.suggested_fix: Verify that auto-logout.service.ts properly calls supabase.auth.signOut() which invalidates the session server-side. Ensure: (1) Client-side timer triggers server-side logout, not just local cleanup. (2) All HTTP interceptors immediately clear authentication state upon 401 response. (3) Refresh tokens are also invalidated. If auto-logout is only client-side, add: await this.supabase.auth.signOut(); this.router.navigate(['/login']);

findings.title: Password visibility toggle exposes input value in DOM
findings.description: The password visibility toggle feature switches between input type='password' and type='text', but this could expose passwords if DOM is inspected or if there's a DOM-based XSS vulnerability.

locations.snippet:
<input
                            id="password"
                            [type]="passwordVisible ? 'text' : 'password'"
                            placeholder="Enter your password"
                            [formControl]="password"
                        />

findings.suggested_fix: This is an acceptable UX pattern, but mitigate risks by: (1) Ensuring password value is never logged or stored in memory longer than needed. (2) Add a disclaimer that password visibility is for user convenience only. (3) Consider requiring HTTPS-only and using secure cookie flags. (4) On logout, explicitly clear password FormControl: this.password.reset(); (5) Never cache passwords in sessionStorage or localStorage.

findings.title: No explicit HTTP-only and Secure cookie configuration visible
findings.description: While Supabase handles session cookies internally, there's no evidence that the application is enforcing HTTP-only and Secure flags or validating cookie security policies.

locations.snippet:
import { ApplicationConfig, provideZoneChangeDetection } from '@angular/core'
import { provideRouter } from '@angular/router'
import { provideHttpClient } from '@angular/common/http'

import { routes } from './app.routes'

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
    providers: [
        provideZoneChangeDetection({ eventCoalescing: true }),
        provideRouter(routes),
        provideHttpClient(),
    ],
}

findings.suggested_fix: Add HttpClientXsrfModule and ensure Supabase client is configured with secure defaults: provideHttpClientWithInterceptors([xsrfInterceptor]). In Supabase initialization, verify session storage is set to 'memory' not 'localStorage'. Configure app to require HTTPS in production. Add HTTP security headers in Nginx/Docker config: add_header Strict-Transport-Security 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options 'nosniff' always;

findings.title: No protection against brute force login attempts
findings.description: The login endpoint has no rate limiting, account lockout mechanism, or progressive delay. An attacker can attempt unlimited login tries without consequences.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement client-side rate limiting using a service: export class RateLimitService { private loginAttempts: { [email: string]: { count: number; timestamp: number } } = {}; canAttemptLogin(email: string): boolean { const key = email; const now = Date.now(); if (this.loginAttempts[key] && now - this.loginAttempts[key].timestamp < 900000) { if (this.loginAttempts[key].count >= 5) return false; } return true; } recordAttempt(email: string) { this.loginAttempts[email] = { count: (this.loginAttempts[email]?.count || 0) + 1, timestamp: Date.now() }; } }. Call canAttemptLogin() before handleLogin(). For server-side: use Supabase's built-in auth protection or implement fail2ban rules.

findings.title: Sensitive modal operations lack authorization checks
findings.description: The reconciliation modal that allows admins to void transactions and the product pricing modal allow sensitive operations without re-confirming authorization or checking permissions beyond initial route guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Add server-side authorization checks for sensitive operations: (1) Before calling supabase.resolveMismatch() or supabase.voidSale(), verify user role is admin by calling a protected endpoint. (2) Supabase RLS policies should enforce: CREATE POLICY "Only admins can resolve mismatches" ON mismatches FOR UPDATE USING (auth.jwt() ->> 'role' = 'admin'); (3) Require secondary confirmation using email verification or TOTP for financial transactions. (4) Implement audit logging for all sensitive operations on backend.

findings.title: Sensitive user data stored in localStorage without encryption
findings.description: User credentials and sensitive profile information (user_id, user_name, user_email, user_role) are stored in plaintext in localStorage. This exposes data to XSS attacks and local storage enumeration. localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript code running in the origin and persists across sessions.

locations.snippet:
public name: string = localStorage.getItem('user_name') || ''
email: string = localStorage.getItem('user_email') || ''
id: string = localStorage.getItem('user_id') || ''
created_by: localStorage.getItem('user_id') || "",
if (!this.currentUser) return;

findings.suggested_fix: Replace localStorage with sessionStorage for sensitive data, or better yet, use Angular's state management (signals/services) to hold user context in memory. If persistence is required, implement encryption-at-rest using a library like TweetNaCl.js or libsodium.js. Example: Instead of `localStorage.getItem('user_id')`, use `this.authService.getCurrentUserId()` where the service manages state securely.

findings.title: Missing input validation on reconciliation modal form inputs
findings.description: The reconciliation component accepts manual quantity input without type validation or sanitization. The form uses ngModel binding directly to template without HTML5 input constraints or Angular validation. Negative values are checked only at confirmation stage, allowing malformed data in the form state.

locations.snippet: units

findings.suggested_fix: Add HTML5 input constraints and Angular form validation: (1) Use ReactiveFormsModule with FormControl for manualQty with Validators.min(0), Validators.max(999999), Validators.required. (2) Add step='1' and pattern='[0-9]*' to input. (3) Disable submit button until form is valid. Example: `<input type="number" formControl="manualQtyControl" class="form-input" min="0" max="999999" step="1" required>`

findings.title: Unvalidated product search input allowing potential XSS
findings.description: The products component accepts searchTerm from user input without sanitization and directly filters products based on string matching. While this doesn't directly render untrusted HTML, the pattern is vulnerable if search results are later displayed with interpolation in templates without property binding.

locations.snippet: search

findings.suggested_fix: Implement input sanitization and validation: (1) Add length limits to search input: `maxlength="100"`. (2) Use Angular's DomSanitizer if results must be rendered as HTML (unlikely here). (3) Validate searchTerm on input: `onSearch(event: any) { const value = (event.target.value || '').trim().slice(0, 100); if(/^[a-zA-Z0-9\s\-]*$/.test(value)) { this.searchTerm = value; this.filterProducts(); } }`. (4) Ensure template uses property binding: `{{ product.name }}` (already correct).

findings.title: Missing CSRF protection on state-changing operations
findings.description: The application uses Angular's default HTTP client setup without explicit CSRF token handling in headers. While Supabase handles auth via JWT, state-changing operations like void transactions, product deletion, and reconciliation updates do not include CSRF tokens. The code relies solely on authentication without additional CSRF protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSRF protection via HTTP headers: (1) Configure Angular's HttpClientXsrfModule in app.config.ts: `import { provideHttpClient, withXsrfConfiguration } from '@angular/common/http'; ...provideHttpClient(withXsrfConfiguration({ cookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN', headerName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN' }))`. (2) Ensure backend validates XSRF tokens on state-changing requests. (3) Alternative: Use SameSite=Strict cookies (server-side config) which mitigates CSRF without explicit tokens.

findings.title: Unvalidated object assignment in reconciliation resolution
findings.description: The reconciliation component uses ngModel for form binding without strict type validation. The manualQty field accepts any value from input and is used directly in calculation without type coercion validation. The resolutionNote field is also unvalidated and passed directly to backend.
findings.suggested_fix: Use reactive forms with validators: (1) Replace ngModel with FormGroup: `this.resolutionForm = this.fb.group({ manualQty: [0, [Validators.required, Validators.min(0), Validators.max(999999), Validators.pattern(/^[0-9]+$/)]], resolutionNote: ['', [Validators.maxLength(500)]] })`. (2) In template: `<input type="number" formControlName="manualQty" min="0" max="999999" step="1">`. (3) Validate before submission: `if (this.resolutionForm.invalid) { return; }`. (4) Sanitize note input: `note = note.trim().slice(0, 500);`

findings.title: Unencrypted sensitive data in API responses and state
findings.description: The application receives and stores sensitive financial data (transaction amounts, customer details, stock counts) in component state and displays them in the DOM without explicit encryption or protection. The data flows from Supabase (over HTTPS, which is good) but is stored in plaintext in memory and potentially in browser caches.

locations.snippet:
Total Revenue {{ financials.totalRevenue | currency:'NGN':'symbol-narrow' }}
💵 Cash at Hand {{ financials.cashAtHand | currency:'NGN':'symbol-narrow' }}

findings.suggested_fix: Implement data protection measures: (1) Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to prevent DOM-based data exfiltration: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self';`. (2) Set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate` on responses containing financial data. (3) Add `pragma: no-cache` headers. (4) Clear sensitive state on logout: `this.financials = { totalRevenue: 0, ... }` in logout handler. (5) Consider using Angular's OnDestroy to clear sensitive arrays: `ngOnDestroy() { this.financials = null; }`

findings.title: Unvalidated receipt/invoice data passed to DOM without sanitization
findings.description: The reconciliation and analysis components display invoice data (item summaries, descriptions, product names) directly in templates using string interpolation. While data comes from database, if any field is user-controlled or vulnerable to injection upstream, it could render malicious content.

locations.snippet: {{ m.products?.name }} {{ m.owner_quantity }}

{{ sale.time }} {{ sale.invoice_id }}
{{ sale.staff_name }}
{{ sale.item_summary }}

findings.suggested_fix: Add DomSanitizer checks and input validation at data loading stage: (1) In analysis.component.ts loadHistory(), validate invoice IDs: `const id = (row.invoice_id || '').replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\-_]/g, '') || `UNK-${Date.now()}`;`. (2) For item_summary, truncate and sanitize: `g.item_summary = (g.items.map((i: Sale) => (i.products?.name || '').substring(0, 50)).join(', ')).substring(0, 200);`. (3) In templates, use [textContent] or {{}} with safe values (already done, but validate at source). (4) Add Content Security Policy to prevent inline script execution.

findings.title: Void transaction reason field lacks length and content validation
findings.description: The voidReason input accepts text up to 500 characters potentially with SQL-like or malicious payloads. The validation only checks for minimum length (5 chars) but doesn't sanitize for special characters or SQL injection patterns. This data is sent to the backend without parameterized query verification visible in the frontend.

locations.snippet:
<!-- Void Reason (Appears Only When Voiding) -->
                        <div *ngIf="isVoidingMode" class="void-reason-box">
                            <textarea [(ngModel)]="voidReason" placeholder="Why are you voiding this transaction?"
                                class="form-textarea" rows="3"></textarea>

findings.suggested_fix: Add input sanitization and length validation: (1) In component: `const sanitizedReason = this.voidReason.trim().slice(0, 200).replace(/[<>"'%;()&+]/g, '');` before sending to backend. (2) In template, add maxlength and pattern: `<textarea [(ngModel)]="voidReason" maxlength="200" placeholder="..." class="form-textarea"></textarea>`. (3) Use reactive forms: `reasonControl: ['', [Validators.required, Validators.minLength(5), Validators.maxLength(200), Validators.pattern(/^[a-zA-Z0-9\s\.,\-()]*$/)]]`. (4) Ensure backend also validates reason field with parameterized queries.

findings.title: Missing Content Security Policy headers
findings.description: The application does not implement CSP headers (visible in HTML or server config). This increases risk of XSS attacks, data exfiltration via third-party scripts, and unauthorized API calls. The inline styles and potential for unsafe-inline scripts are not mitigated.

locations.snippet:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">

<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>FrostflowApp</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="favicon.ico" />
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" rel="preconnect" />
    <link crossorigin="" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" rel="preconnect" />
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
        rel="stylesheet" />
    <link
        href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Material+Symbols+Outlined:wght,FILL@100..700,0..1&display=swap"
        rel="stylesheet" />
    <!-- Add this line for Font Awesome -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.min.css" />

findings.suggested_fix: Add CSP meta tag in index.html head and configure server headers: (1) Add to <head> in src/index.html: `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co https://api.supabase.co; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self';">`. (2) Configure in Nginx/Docker: Add `add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; ...";` to server block. (3) Add additional headers: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`.

findings.title: Unvalidated numerical input in expense and stock calculations
findings.description: The analysis component calculates financial metrics (totalSpent, netProfit) from database values without validating that amounts are valid positive numbers. If backend data is corrupted or user manipulates data upstream, calculations could produce NaN or Infinity values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add numeric validation and bounds checking: (1) Validate each value: `const cost = typeof e.total_cost === 'number' && e.total_cost >= 0 ? e.total_cost : 0;`. (2) Add max value checks: `if (cost > 999999999) cost = 999999999;`. (3) After calculation, validate result: `this.expenseMetrics.netProfit = Math.max(-999999999, Math.min(999999999, this.financials.totalRevenue - total));`. (4) Add Number.isFinite() checks: `if (!Number.isFinite(total)) { total = 0; }`. (5) Example: `const cost = Math.max(0, Math.min(999999999, parseFloat(e.total_cost) || 0));`

findings.title: Hardcoded CDN URL for external scripts without integrity checks
findings.description: The application loads Chart.js from CDN without Subresource Integrity (SRI) verification. If the CDN is compromised or MITM attack occurs, malicious script could be loaded. Font Awesome and Google Fonts are also loaded from external sources without SRI.

locations.snippet: <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.min.css" />

findings.suggested_fix: Add Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes and verify remote sources: (1) For Chart.js, add integrity hash: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.5.1" integrity="sha384-<HASH>" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>` (get hash from jsDelivr or npm). (2) For Font Awesome: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.min.css" integrity="sha384-<HASH>" crossorigin="anonymous">`. (3) For Google Fonts, add nonce or preload: `<link rel="preload" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?..." as="style">`. (4) Update CSP to require SRI: `script-src 'self' https: 'require-sri-for-script';`. (5) Prefer npm packages over CDN when possible.

findings.title: No validation on product image URLs before rendering
findings.description: The products component displays product images from database URLs without validation or sanitization. Malicious users with database access could inject data: URIs, javascript: protocols, or third-party tracking URLs that could exfiltrate user data or execute scripts.

locations.snippet: image
image

findings.suggested_fix: Validate and sanitize image URLs before rendering: (1) In ProductsComponent constructor, inject DomSanitizer: `constructor(private sanitizer: DomSanitizer) {}`. (2) Create a sanitization method: `getSafeImageUrl(url: string | null | undefined): SafeUrl { if (!url || typeof url !== 'string') return this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustUrl(''); const validated = /^https:\/\//.test(url) && !url.includes('javascript:') && !url.includes('data:') ? url : ''; return this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustUrl(validated); }`. (3) In template: ``. (4) Better: Use CSP `img-src 'self' https://trusted-domain.com;` to whitelist allowed image sources.

findings.title: Unvalidated modal element ID concatenation creating potential DOM-based XSS
findings.description: The reconciliation component creates dynamic element IDs by concatenating data without sanitization. If mismatch.id contains special characters, it could break out of the ID attribute and inject attributes or event handlers.

locations.snippet: <tr *ngFor="let m of mismatches" [id]="'mismatch-' + m.id" [class.highlight]="highlightId == m.id">

findings.suggested_fix: Validate and sanitize ID values: (1) In ReconciliationComponent.loadData(), sanitize IDs: `const sanitizedId = (m.id || '').replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\-_]/g, '').substring(0, 50) || `mismatch-${index}`;`. (2) Store cleaned ID in mismatch object. (3) In template: `[id]="'mismatch-' + (m.id | slice:0:50)"` or use *ngFor index: `[id]="'mismatch-' + $index"`. (4) In component: Use template reference instead of direct DOM access: `<tr #mismatchRow [id]="'mismatch-' + m.id">` and `@ViewChild('mismatchRow') mismatchRow: HTMLTableRowElement;`. (5) Better approach: `const el = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-mismatch-id]')).find(e => e.getAttribute('data-mismatch-id') === this.highlightId);`

findings.title: Missing HTTPS enforcement and security headers configuration
findings.description: The application lacks explicit HTTPS enforcement, HSTS headers, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and other critical security headers. The index.html loads external resources (Google Fonts, FontAwesome CDN, Chart.js CDN) over HTTPS but there's no Content-Security-Policy configured. Angular production builds don't automatically enforce these headers without explicit server configuration.

locations.snippet:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>FrostflowApp</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="favicon.ico" />
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" rel="preconnect" />
    <link crossorigin="" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" rel="preconnect" />

findings.suggested_fix: Add security headers via Nginx configuration in Docker setup: Add 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' for HSTS, 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff', 'X-Frame-Options: DENY', 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin'. Implement Content-Security-Policy header restricting scripts to 'self' and trusted CDN origins. Add meta tags in index.html: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:;">

findings.title: Sensitive data stored in localStorage without encryption
findings.description: User credentials and profile information (user_id, user_name, user_email, user_role) are stored in plaintext localStorage. This is vulnerable to XSS attacks and can leak sensitive information if browser storage is compromised. localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript in the same origin, including malicious scripts injected via XSS.

locations.snippet:
public name: string = localStorage.getItem('user_name') || ''
    email: string = localStorage.getItem('user_email') || ''
    id: string = localStorage.getItem('user_id') || ''
const role = localStorage.getItem('user_role');

findings.suggested_fix: Replace localStorage with sessionStorage for temporary session data. Never store sensitive credentials in any client-side storage. Instead: (1) Use JWT tokens with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies managed by the browser, (2) Retrieve user profile from authenticated endpoints on app load, (3) Store non-sensitive state in sessionStorage only if necessary, (4) Consider using Angular's memory-based state management (signals/services) for runtime data. Remove all localStorage.setItem calls for sensitive data from login/auth flow.

findings.title: No rate limiting on API endpoints
findings.description: The Supabase service makes multiple API calls (authentication, data queries, realtime subscriptions) without apparent rate limiting. No throttling mechanism is visible in the SupabaseService, and Angular HttpClient is configured without rate limit interceptors. This exposes the application to brute-force attacks, DOS, and resource exhaustion.

locations.snippet:
async loadData() {
        this.isLoading = true
        this.mismatches = await this.supabase.getPendingMismatches()
        this.totalMismatches = this.mismatches.length
        this.criticalItems = this.mismatches.filter(
            (m) => m.difference > 5
        ).length
        this.isLoading = false

findings.suggested_fix: Implement rate limiting at multiple layers: (1) In HttpClient interceptor: Use RxJS debounceTime/throttleTime operators to limit request frequency, (2) Add exponential backoff retry logic, (3) Implement login attempt rate limiting (max 5 attempts per 15 minutes), (4) Server-side: Configure Supabase Realtime connection limits and query rate limiting, (5) Add client-side request queuing with max concurrent requests. Example interceptor: `provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([rateLimitInterceptor]))` using custom interceptor that tracks request counts and rejects excessive requests.

findings.title: CORS configuration not visible - potential origin bypass
findings.description: No explicit CORS configuration is visible in the provided code. The application uses Supabase backend but Angular's HttpClient default CORS policy and Supabase's CORS settings are not documented. Without explicit CORS configuration, the application may be vulnerable to cross-origin attacks or overly permissive configurations.
findings.suggested_fix: Define explicit CORS configuration: (1) In Supabase project settings, restrict allowed origins to production domain only (never allow wildcard '*'), (2) In Angular HttpClient interceptor, ensure credentials are sent with requests: `withCredentials: true`, (3) Document CORS policy in deployment configuration, (4) Add CORS validation tests. Example: `provideHttpClient(withXsrfConfiguration({cookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN', headerName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN'}))`. For Docker/Nginx deployment, add: `add_header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' 'https://yourdomain.com' always;`

findings.title: External CDN dependencies without Subresource Integrity (SRI)
findings.description: The application loads Chart.js from CDN (cdn.jsdelivr.net) and FontAwesome (cdnjs.cloudflare.com) in index.html without Subresource Integrity hashes. This makes the application vulnerable to CDN compromise attacks where malicious code could be injected.

locations.snippet:
<!-- Add this line for Font Awesome -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.min.css" />
</head>

<body>
    <app-root></app-root>
    <!-- Chart.js CDN (used instead of installing via npm to avoid dependency conflicts) -->
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js"></script>

findings.suggested_fix: Add Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes to all external resources: For Chart.js: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js" integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>` (replace ... with actual hash). For FontAwesome: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.min.css" integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous">`. Better approach: Install dependencies via npm (chart.js and font-awesome packages) to include them in your bundle instead of using CDN, eliminating CDN risk.

findings.title: Verbose error messages exposed to users in production
findings.description: Error handling in multiple components logs full error objects and stack traces to console and toast notifications. In reconciliation.component.ts line 168 and analysis.component.ts, errors are caught and displayed with potentially sensitive details. Production users could see database errors, API paths, and implementation details.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement proper error handling: (1) In production, show generic error messages to users ('An error occurred. Please try again.' or 'Unable to save changes'), (2) Log detailed errors server-side only (via error logging service like Sentry), (3) Remove console.error calls or wrap in development-only checks: `if (!environment.production) console.error(error)`, (4) Never expose error.message to UI, (5) Create error boundary service that maps backend error codes to user-friendly messages. Example: `private handleError(error: any) { if (environment.production) { return 'An unexpected error occurred'; } return error.message; }`

findings.title: Debug mode potentially enabled in production
findings.description: The README mentions 'Angular v19+' and app.component.ts initializes multiple debug-friendly subscriptions and signal effects. No environment-specific configuration visible that would disable debug features in production builds. Source maps may be exposed in production bundle.
findings.suggested_fix: Create environment files: (1) Add `src/environments/environment.ts` (dev) and `src/environments/environment.prod.ts` (prod), (2) Set `production: false/true` flags, (3) In production config: `sourceMap: false, optimization: true, outputHashing: 'all'`, (4) Update angular.json to use environment files in configuration, (5) Conditionally enable console logs: `if (!environment.production) console.log()`, (6) In tsconfig.prod.json add optimization flags. Ensure build command uses: `ng build --configuration production`.

findings.title: Known vulnerable dependency versions
findings.description: package.json uses @supabase/supabase-js@^2.81.1 with npm override for @supabase/gotrue-js@2.61.0. The caret (^) allows minor version updates. Chart.js@^4.5.1, RxJS@~7.8.0 are specified with loose versioning. No lock file security audit visible. Potential known CVEs in transitive dependencies.

locations.snippet:
"dependencies": {
        "@angular/common": "^19.2.0",
        "@angular/compiler": "^19.2.0",
        "@angular/core": "^19.2.0",
        "@supabase/supabase-js": "^2.81.1",
        "chart.js": "^4.5.1",
        "random-verse": "^1.0.1",
        "rxjs": "~7.8.0",

findings.suggested_fix: Implement dependency security management: (1) Run `npm audit` and `npm audit fix` to resolve known vulnerabilities, (2) Use exact versions for critical dependencies (replace ^ and ~ with =): `@supabase/supabase-js: 2.81.1`, (3) Add pre-commit hook using husky: `npm install husky --save-dev && husky install`, (4) Configure GitHub Dependabot or npm audit CI/CD checks, (5) Remove 'random-verse' dependency if not critical (it's unused), (6) Add `npm ci` instead of `npm install` in Docker builds to use lock file. In CI/CD: add `- run: npm audit --audit-level=moderate` step.

findings.title: Missing request timeout configuration
findings.description: Angular HttpClient is configured without explicit timeout settings. Long-running requests or network hangs could leave connections open indefinitely, consuming resources and enabling slowloris-style DOS attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add HTTP timeout configuration with interceptor: (1) Create custom HTTP interceptor that adds timeout: `timeout(30000)` (30 seconds), (2) Apply to all HTTP calls: `provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([timeoutInterceptor]))`, (3) For critical API calls, use shorter timeouts. Example interceptor: `export function timeoutInterceptor(req: HttpRequest<any>, next: HttpHandlerFn) { return next(req).pipe(timeout(30000)); }` or use `req.clone()` with explicit settings. Consider different timeouts: file uploads (60s), normal API (30s), login (15s).

findings.title: No CSRF protection configured
findings.description: Angular provides built-in CSRF protection via HttpClientXsrfModule, but there's no visible configuration in app.config.ts or mention of CSRF tokens in API calls. The backend Supabase authentication may handle some CSRF protection, but explicit client-side configuration is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CSRF protection: (1) In app.config.ts, add XSRF configuration: `withXsrfConfiguration({ cookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN', headerName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN' })`, (2) Ensure backend sets XSRF-TOKEN cookie with SameSite=Strict, (3) For state-changing operations (POST, PUT, DELETE), verify XSRF token is sent in headers. Updated config: `provideHttpClient(withXsrfConfiguration({cookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN', headerName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN'}), withInterceptors([...]))`

findings.title: No Content Security Policy (CSP) headers configured
findings.description: Application loads external resources (Google Fonts, FontAwesome CDN, Chart.js) but has no CSP header to restrict script/style sources. This leaves the app vulnerable to XSS and malicious injection attacks.

locations.snippet:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>FrostflowApp</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="favicon.ico" />

findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSP headers: (1) Add to index.html meta tag or configure in Nginx/Docker: `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com;">`, (2) In Nginx add header: `add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com 'unsafe-inline';" always;`, (3) Consider moving to 'unsafe-inline' alternatives using nonce attributes for dynamic styles.

findings.title: Unused dependency 'random-verse' increases attack surface
findings.description: package.json includes 'random-verse@^1.0.1' which appears unused in the codebase (no import statements found). Including unused dependencies increases the dependency tree size and potential vulnerability surface.

locations.snippet: "random-verse": "^1.0.1",

findings.suggested_fix: Remove unused dependency: Run `npm uninstall random-verse` and remove from package.json. Verify it's not imported anywhere with: `grep -r 'random-verse' src/`. This reduces dependency footprint and maintenance burden.

findings.title: Overly permissive TypeScript configuration may hide type errors
findings.description: tsconfig.json uses `skipLibCheck: true` which skips type checking for declaration files. This can hide vulnerabilities in type definitions and third-party packages. Using `strict: true` but with skipLibCheck reduces effectiveness.

locations.snippet:
"compilerOptions": {
        "outDir": "./dist/out-tsc",
        "strict": true,
        "noImplicitOverride": true,
        "noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": true,
        "noImplicitReturns": true,
        "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
        "skipLibCheck": true,

findings.suggested_fix: Review skipLibCheck necessity: Consider setting `skipLibCheck: false` to enable full type checking, or if necessary, use `skipDefaultLibCheck: true` instead (faster, checks only necessary libs). For critical security builds, enable all type checks: set `skipLibCheck: false` in CI/CD pipeline at least.

findings.title: No auto-logout timeout visible in configuration
findings.description: While auto-logout service exists (auto-logout.service.ts mentioned), timeout duration is not configurable or visible in settings. Default timeout values could be too long or users can't adjust for security-sensitive environments.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure explicit auto-logout timeout: (1) Create environment-based configuration: `export const SESSION_TIMEOUT = environment.production ? 15 * 60 * 1000 : 30 * 60 * 1000` (15min prod, 30min dev), (2) Make timeout configurable per role: admin 15min, sales 30min, (3) Warn users before timeout (5-min warning dialog), (4) Update AutoLogoutService to use this config value. Document timeout values in security policy.

findings.title: Missing pagination on products list
findings.description: The products.component.ts loads all products without any pagination. For large product catalogs, this will cause significant performance degradation with thousands of records fetched simultaneously.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement server-side pagination in ProductService with limit/offset or cursor-based pagination. Add pagination controls to the template with page size of 20-50 items.

findings.title: No caching for dashboard metrics API calls
findings.description: DashboardMetricsComponent makes two separate API calls (getDashboardMetrics, getSalesDashboardMetrics) every time the component initializes. These values change infrequently but are fetched repeatedly on navigation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add caching to SupabaseService methods with a TTL (e.g., 5 minutes) using RxJS shareReplay or a simple Map-based cache. Reuse cached data if available and not expired.

findings.title: Missing pagination on sales history
findings.description: The analysis component loads all sales history for a given month without pagination. For high-volume retail, this could result in hundreds or thousands of records being loaded at once.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement pagination in getSalesHistory with page/limit parameters. Load initial 50 records and implement infinite scroll or pagination controls for additional pages.

findings.title: Unbounded realtime subscription without throttling
findings.description: The owner-dashboard subscribes to notifications via realtime but loads all unread notifications on init without limiting the result set. Additionally, the activity feed loads last 10 sales with no pagination controls.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .limit(50) or similar to notification queries. Consider adding a 'load more' mechanism for activity feeds.

findings.title: Repeated computation in filter loop
findings.description: The products component filters all products on every search input change without debouncing. This causes unnecessary recalculation on each keystroke.
findings.suggested_fix: Add debounce (300ms) to the onSearch method using RxJS debounceTime operator. This prevents filtering on every keystroke.

findings.title: Missing OnPush change detection strategy
findings.description: Components use default change detection which causes unnecessary re-renders. The dashboard-metrics, activity-feed, and stock-alerts components would benefit from OnPush strategy.
findings.suggested_fix: Add changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to all display-only components. This reduces change detection cycles significantly.

findings.title: No eager loading of relations in queries
findings.description: The sales history query appears to fetch raw data then map it, but likely doesn't use Supabase's select with related tables (products, users). This causes potential N+1 pattern when accessing s.users?.name and s.products?.name in templates.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Supabase's .select('*, products(*), users(*)') or equivalent to eagerly load related tables in a single query instead of separate requests.

findings.title: Multiple sequential async calls in component init
findings.description: Analysis component makes 5 sequential await calls in ngOnInit, blocking UI render until all complete. These could be parallelized with Promise.all.
findings.suggested_fix: The Promise.all is good but getCurrentUser() is outside it. Move getCurrentUser() inside Promise.all or use Promise.allSettled to prevent one failure from blocking others.

findings.title: Realtime subscriptions without cleanup guarantee
findings.description: StockAlertsComponent starts listening in ngOnInit but the stopListening() is called in ngOnDestroy. If component is destroyed before data loads, there could be a race condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider using a subject with takeUntilDestroyed() or a similar pattern to ensure cleanup happens reliably. Also, verify that startListening() properly handles multiple calls.

findings.title: God module: supabase.service.ts exceeds 800 LOC with mixed responsibilities
findings.description: The Supabase service file contains 847 lines of code handling authentication, data access, webhook management, and business logic all in a single service. This violates single responsibility principle and makes the module difficult to test and maintain. Multiple unrelated concerns (auth, CRUD operations, webhook handling) are tightly coupled together.

findings.suggested_fix: Split into domain-specific services: AuthService (auth logic), ProductDataService (product CRUD), SalesDataService (sales operations), InventoryDataService (stock management), ReconciliationDataService, and WebhookService (already exists but logic may be duplicated)

findings.description: Multiple page components (sales-dashboard, inventory, products, reconciliation, analysis, staff, owner-dashboard) directly inject and call the monolithic Supabase service. This creates tight coupling between presentation layer and data access, making it difficult to swap implementations, test components in isolation, or refactor data access patterns.

findings.title: Inconsistent service architecture: ProductService exists but logic may be duplicated in SupabaseService
findings.description: ProductService (149 LOC) exists alongside SupabaseService, but unclear separation of responsibilities. Components may be calling both services or the pattern is inconsistently applied across the codebase. This creates confusion about which service should be used for product operations.

findings.title: Sales-management module lacks cohesion with 4 distinct components handling related concerns
findings.description: The sales-management module (800 LOC, 16 files) contains 4 separate components (sales-dashboard, sales-history, sales-lookup, sales-receive) that appear to handle different aspects of sales but lack clear service layer abstraction. Components likely duplicate similar Supabase calls and business logic. No shared sales service layer to coordinate these concerns.

findings.suggested_fix: Create SalesService facade that coordinates sales operations across dashboard, history, and receive functionality. Extract shared queries and mutations to service. Components should use SalesService instead of direct Supabase calls.

findings.title: Layout and UI components tightly coupled with business logic containers
findings.description: Layout components (sidebar, admin-layout, main-layout) are located in src/app/components/ alongside UI components (loading, toast, dashboard-metrics, stock-alerts, activity-feed). Layout containers that manage business state should be separated from pure UI components. Current organization makes it unclear which components handle presentation vs. state management.

locations.snippet: Mixed layout containers and UI components: sidebar (18 LOC), admin-layout (13 LOC), main-layout (36 LOC) alongside dashboard-metrics (29 LOC), stock-alerts (32 LOC), activity-feed (40 LOC)

findings.suggested_fix: Reorganize: Move layout components to src/app/layouts/ or src/app/shell/. Keep src/app/components/ for pure presentational/shared UI components. Consider nesting smart components with their related smart components.

findings.title: Analysis component (292 LOC) has large TypeScript footprint suggesting mixed responsibilities
findings.description: The analysis component contains 292 lines of TypeScript logic alongside 464 lines of HTML and 1128 lines of CSS. This suggests the component may be handling AI report generation logic, data transformation, visualization setup, and presentation—multiple responsibilities that should be separated.

locations.snippet: Large component combining presentation and business logic

findings.suggested_fix: Extract AI report generation and data transformation logic into AnalysisService. Create smaller presentational sub-components for report display sections. Component should only handle view state and delegate to service for calculations and API calls.

findings.title: Authentication logic scattered across multiple locations
findings.description: Auth logic is spread across: auth.guard.ts (37 LOC), login.component.ts (68 LOC), and likely within supabase.service.ts (847 LOC). No centralized AuthService facade exists, making it unclear where authentication state is managed and how to extend auth functionality consistently.

findings.suggested_fix: Create centralized AuthenticationService that consolidates: login/logout logic, session management, token refresh, and auth state. Auth guard and login component should use AuthenticationService exclusively. Move auth-related logic from SupabaseService to AuthenticationService.

findings.title: Webhook and notification services lack clear abstraction boundaries
findings.description: WebhookService (40 LOC), ToastService (32 LOC), and notification-related logic may be scattered. Unclear how external webhooks, internal notifications, and user-facing toasts coordinate. Potential for duplicate notification handling logic.

locations.snippet: Webhook integration service

findings.suggested_fix: Establish clear notification flow: External events → WebhookService → internal domain events → ToastService (for UI feedback). Document when each service should be used. Consider creating NotificationCoordinatorService if cross-cutting logic exists.

findings.title: Cross-cutting concerns (Loading, AutoLogout, PageReload) lack centralized orchestration
findings.description: Three utility services manage application-wide concerns: LoadingService (26 LOC), AutoLogoutService (74 LOC), PageReloadService (71 LOC). These services likely have complex interdependencies and subscribe to shared state but lack orchestration. No clear owner for managing their lifecycle and interactions.

locations.snippet: Global loading state

Page reload and state management

findings.suggested_fix: Create AppStateService or StateOrchestrationService that manages loading, session, and page state as cohesive unit. These utilities should not directly manage global state independently but coordinate through central service.

findings.title: Missing repository pattern for data persistence abstraction
findings.description: All data access goes directly through SupabaseService without repository pattern. No abstraction layer between business logic (components/services) and Supabase SDK. If database provider needs to change (e.g., from Supabase to Firebase), all components and services require modification.

locations.snippet: Direct Supabase SDK usage throughout

findings.suggested_fix: Implement Repository pattern with typed repositories for each domain entity: ProductRepository, SalesRepository, InventoryRepository, etc. These should abstract Supabase SDK and expose domain-specific methods. Facilitates testing with mock repositories and easier migration to different backends.

codebase_map.architecture_summary: A full-stack Angular 19 SPA application for inventory and sales management (FrostFlow). Uses Supabase as BaaS for PostgreSQL database, authentication, and realtime subscriptions. Features role-based access (Admin, Staff) via auth guards. Multiple business modules: sales tracking, inventory management, reconciliation, AI-powered analytics, and staff management. Supports webhook integrations and includes dashboard metrics visualization with Chart.js.
